target.artifact: portfolio job/dedupe-key live-claim mutual exclusion fence

title: Fence concurrent portfolio claims per dedupe key
problem: The v1.1 portfolio contract requires an atomic claim before work, but the append-only claim path includes a unique claim_id. Under concurrent fresh-chat launches, two workers can both create different files for the same job and dedupe_key, so neither create collides. Live evidence on 2026-09-17 shows two claims for portfolio-tele-recover-intent-and-artifacts created eight seconds apart. Without a second atomic exclusivity primitive, both can legally proceed into duplicate archaeology/implementation.
mission: Add a job/dedupe-key exclusivity fence to portfolio acquisition while retaining append-only immutable claim history. Acquisition must fail closed for losers, support safe expiry/recovery, and be falsified with a concurrent race fixture before the contract can call portfolio claim exclusivity operational.
acceptance: For one portfolio dedupe_key, concurrent contenders cannot both acquire substantive-work authority while one live claim is unexpired.
The exclusivity decision uses atomic create-if-absent or CAS on a shared deterministic fence identity, not unique append-only filenames alone.
Append-only claim files remain immutable historical evidence and identify the authoritative fence generation/owner.
An expired owner can be replaced only through an explicit CAS/recovery generation; timestamps alone never overwrite a live owner.
A losing contender records or can reconstruct the winner, performs no substantive target writes, and immediately re-enters allocation.
Terminal returns and existing derived-job dedupe rules remain compatible.
A two-or-more-worker concurrency fixture reproduces the current double-claim race before the repair and demonstrates exactly one authoritative owner after the repair.

observed_live_evidence.finding: Two unique append-only claim creates succeeded for the same job/dedupe frontier; unique claim_id paths do not provide job-level mutual exclusion.

value_signals.unblock_value: Makes portfolio fallback safe under the exact many-chat load pattern /wc v3.3 is designed to support.
value_signals.compounding_value: Every seed and derived portfolio job benefits; duplicate-work risk otherwise rises as worker count rises.
value_signals.human_friction_reduction: Workers can resolve portfolio claim races without the human choosing which chat should continue.
value_signals.information_gain: A deterministic fence plus race fixture converts an observed concurrency defect into measurable pass/fail canary evidence.

risk.main: A coarse permanent lock could strand a job after worker death or serialize unrelated dedupe keys.
risk.mitigation: Fence by stable dedupe-key/job identity, preserve expiry metadata, and require CAS-controlled generation handoff for stale/expired ownership rather than overwrite-by-recency.

falsification: Two concurrent contenders for the same dedupe_key both obtain substantive-work authority.
A contender can replace an unexpired owner merely because its timestamp is newer.
An expired lock cannot be safely advanced without deleting historical claim evidence.
The fence blocks a different portfolio dedupe_key from progressing in parallel.
The repair requires rewriting or deleting immutable historical claim files.
dedup_note: Distinct from P-1c64c0e1e704-recovery-race-v1, which fences stale-recovery writers in the normal opportunity recovery fabric. This proposal targets the new portfolio fallback claim protocol and is grounded by two same-job portfolio claims observed after /wc v3.3 rollout.

source_freshness.note: Main was highly concurrent during the canary; evidence paths were reloaded directly from current main immediately before discovery pinning.
